findings.claim: Endpoint-integrated contrasts are strongest and most consistent for shape descriptors: shape_yy shows a negative high-low integrated contrast (z=-0.51, q=1.5e-5, 0/14 positive batches) and shape_xx is similarly negative (z=-0.50, q=8.1e-4, 1/14 positive). These are signed favorable-versus-comparison coordinate contrasts at the observed endpoint, not absolute geometric descriptors.

Global centroid contrasts are weak and mostly null: centroid_x (z=-0.11, q=0.26) and centroid_z (z=-0.06, q=0.48) are not distinguishable from zero, while centroid_y is negative but modest (z=-0.24, q=0.014, 3/14 positive). Centroid position is therefore a poor priority relative to shape contrasts.

Continuous landmark contrasts are non-monotone across the observed window: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z=+9.27 and last_rate_z=-10.00, and landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z=-72.4 and last_rate_z=+5.5. No polynomial was accepted and extrapolation is disallowed, so a constant rule is not supported over the observed support.

Several landmark local contrasts show strong sign conflicts (landmark_00_local_dx: 9 strong_sign_conflicts, 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dz: 7 conflicts, 10 sign changes), indicating unstable direction evidence within the observed window rather than a coherent marginal descriptor.

The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary with validity and strain secondary under coordinate-only control; the observed endpoint contrasts above are coordinate rewards, not physical interaction energies or affinity-head derivatives.

hypotheses.falsifier: A constant rule matching or exceeding the time-conditioned rule on held-out observed nodes, or accepted polynomial fit removing the sign changes.
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule that follows the observed-node sign of landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_00_local_dy will track the endpoint contrast better than a constant rule, because both features reverse rate sign within the observed window.

hypotheses.falsifier: Batch-resampled sign reversal or q-value rising above the declared threshold.
hypotheses.observable: endpoint high-low integrated z for shape_yy and shape_xx
hypotheses.statement: Shape_yy and shape_xx negative endpoint contrasts are the most reliable signed coordinate directions for prioritization, given their multiplicity-adjusted significance and near-uniform negative batch fraction.

limitations: No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data were supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.
No covariance, intact-conformation or mode diagnostics were read, so coherent joint-pattern versus isolated-marginal coupling could not be assessed.
No parent-child increment or turnover residual evidence was read, so within-path change versus changing cohort composition is unresolved.
Continuous contrasts are coordinate rewards only; they are not absolute reward targets or physical interaction energies.
